outcome: mode of delivery (cesarean section vs. vaginal)
cohort: The study included 190 primigravid women with a singleton pregnancy at term and vertex presentation.
finding: Maternal anthropometric parameters, including height, Bisacromial Diameter, Intercristal Diameter, Intertrochanteric Diameter, and foot length, were significantly associated with cephalopelvic disproportion (CPD) in primigravid women.
mod_finding: Maternal height and other anthropometric measurements were found to be helpful in determining cephalopelvic disproportion, which often necessitates delivery by cesarean section.
cross-section timing: Data was collected from primigravid women at term, correlating maternal anthropometric parameters with the mode of delivery.
